target.title: fix: pace delivery recovery after startup outages
target.body:
Closes #101058

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where startup delivery recovery could replay many already-eligible queued messages in a tight burst after an outage or restart. That burst can concentrate outbound sends against channel/provider rate limits even though each individual delivery is retried sequentially.

## Why This Change Was Made

Startup recovery now applies a small shared pacing delay between actual replay attempts for outbound deliveries and session deliveries. Backoff skips, max-retry moves, reconnect drains, and first-entry recovery semantics stay unchanged; the delay is also bounded by the existing recovery deadline so startup recovery still defers cleanly when its budget is exhausted.

## User Impact

Queued messages recovered after a restart are replayed more gently instead of all eligible entries being sent back-to-back. This should reduce avoidable 429s and temporary outbound delivery failures after longer outages while preserving existing retry and reconnect behavior.

## Evidence

Before premise, source at base `60ce506712295e03d53cd4b91f4472f61d5971a6`: `recoverPendingDeliveries` sorted pending entries and immediately iterated them with `for (const entry of pending)` before calling `drainQueuedEntry`; `recoverPendingSessionDeliveries` had the same tight startup loop. There was no sleep, pacing helper, or jitter between eligible replays.
